what_its_for: Silver sulfadiazine is a cream used to prevent and treat infections in people with serious burns. It kills bacteria and other germs that can infect burned skin and helps protect the wound while it heals.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before and after applying this cream. Clean and rinse the burned area as directed by your healthcare provider. Using a sterile glove or clean applicator, apply a thin layer of cream (about as thick as a nickel) over the entire burned area. Cover the treated area with a sterile bandage or dressing as instructed. Apply the cream once or twice daily, or as directed. Do not skip applications, as keeping the wound covered with cream at all times is important to prevent infection.
dosing: Apply a layer about 1/16 inch (1.5 mm) thick once or twice daily, or as your doctor or nurse tells you. Your healthcare team will likely change your dressing and reapply cream during your wound care visits. Always follow the exact schedule your care team gives you.
missed_dose: If you miss an application, apply the cream as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next scheduled application, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed dose. Contact your healthcare provider if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store silver sulfadiazine cream at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and freezing temperatures. Keep the lid tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children. Do not use the cream if it has turned dark or changed color, as this may mean it is no longer effective.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this cream in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Do not use other creams, ointments, or wound products on the same area unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid exposing treated areas to sunlight, as burned skin is very sensitive. Do not use this cream if you are allergic to sulfa drugs without talking to your doctor first. Avoid using this cream near the end of pregnancy (last few weeks) or on newborn babies unless specifically directed by a doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or nurse right away if you notice: signs of infection such as increased redness, swelling, warmth, pus, or a bad smell from the wound; a rash, itching, or hives not related to the burn; skin turning bluish-gray (a rare side effect called argyria); fever or chills; unusual bruising or bleeding; difficulty breathing; or if the wound does not seem to be healing or is getting worse. Also call if you develop signs of a kidney or liver problem such as decreased urination, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual fatigue.
when_it_works: Silver sulfadiazine starts working to kill germs right away after it is applied. However, healing from a serious burn takes time — often several weeks or even months depending on how large and deep the burn is. You may not see visible improvement right away, but the cream is working to protect your wound from infection while your body heals. Keep using it as directed even if the wound looks the same or you do not feel a difference.
special_populations: Pregnant women: Avoid use during the last weeks of pregnancy as it may harm the newborn baby. Newborns and premature infants: This cream should generally not be used on newborns or premature babies due to risk of a serious blood condition called kernicterus. Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially kidney-related effects. People with kidney or liver disease: Your doctor will monitor you more closely, as this drug can sometimes affect kidney and liver function. People with G6PD deficiency: Use with caution, as this medication may cause a type of anemia. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and medications before using this cream.
